reason: This Hebrew text (Exodus 2:16-22) is a narrative passage describing Moses meeting Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, at a well. The passage recounts how Moses helped the daughters draw water, was invited to stay with their father Reuel, married Zipporah, and had a son named Gershom. The passage contains no theological statements about Yahweh's loyalty to the people, covenant obligations, or any consideration of replacing Israel with another people. It is purely biographical narrative with no divine commentary.
